title: Highest temperature in London on September 3?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official Met Office guidance and supporting model runs project a daytime maximum near 26 °C for London on 3 September, with hourly profiles peaking in the mid-afternoon under a mix of sunny intervals and variable cloud. Westerly flow advecting milder Atlantic air, combined with limited daytime heating from partial cloud cover and moderate wind speeds, supports this narrow 25–26 °C band as the most probable outcome. Recent model consensus has remained stable over the past 24–48 hours, with only minor spreads between GFS and ECMWF solutions that keep 27 °C or higher as lower-probability outliers. The market-implied odds align closely with this forecast distribution, reflecting traders’ weighting of official agency data and the narrow uncertainty range typical for a 24-hour horizon.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Paris-Le Bourget Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lfpb

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from models like GFS indicate a highest temperature in Paris on September 3 centered around 25–27 °C under partly to mostly cloudy skies with moderate westerly flow. This positioning stems from stable high-pressure influence and lack of strong warm-air advection, keeping daytime maxima close to or slightly above the 23 °C seasonal average. Low precipitation odds and consistent model agreement limit upside risk for 28 °C or higher, while the 19.5 % probability on 25 °C or below reflects minor cooling potential from increased cloud cover. Traders are weighting the latest runs showing peak readings near 26–27 °C, aligning market-implied odds with observed forecast consensus.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and supporting models position 30–32°C as the most probable range for Tokyo’s daily maximum on September 3, 2026.** 

The JMA’s September 2 update calls for a mostly cloudy day with rain developing later, especially from midday onward, and assigns a 30°C maximum (some local media citing 31°C). Multiple private forecasts converge on highs of 28–31°C (roughly 82–88°F), with afternoon showers and thunderstorms limiting peak heating. Southerly flow ahead of an approaching front maintains moisture and cloud cover, while the timing of precipitation reduces insolation during the warmest hours. 

This setup follows a warm September 2 (observed max near 32–33°C) and aligns with early-September climatology, where daily normals sit around 29–30°C but convective activity frequently caps extremes. Model consensus shows limited upside beyond 32°C once rain begins, while downside below 29°C would require earlier or heavier precipitation than currently indicated. The market’s heavy weighting on 30°C (23.5%) and 31°C (36.0%), followed by 32°C (22.0%), directly reflects this narrow forecast envelope and the modest uncertainty around exact rain onset and intensity. Updated JMA or numerical guidance in the next 12–18 hours will be the key catalyst for any shifts in implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus for Shenzhen on September 3, 2026, centers on a daily high of 29–31°C, directly explaining the market's concentration on those outcomes (30°C at 41%, 31°C at 26%, 29°C at 16.5%).** Multiple meteorological sources, including local Chinese weather services and international models, project highs near 30°C under mostly cloudy conditions with thundershowers or moderate rain, northwest winds under 3–10 m/s, and high humidity (70–85%). 

These conditions stem from Shenzhen’s humid subtropical monsoon climate in early September, where seasonal moisture and cloud cover typically cap daytime maxima around the 30°C mark rather than allowing stronger heating. Recent observations from September 2 show similar patterns—overcast skies, light rain, and temperatures peaking at 30–31°C—reinforcing model runs that limit further warming. 

The slight edge for 30°C reflects the most common forecast value across ensembles, while spread to 29°C or 31°C accounts for shower timing and local variability; probabilities drop sharply above 32°C due to expected rain suppression and below 28°C given persistent warmth. Updated model guidance and official briefings on September 3 morning will provide the final observational data for market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Incoming cold front and associated precipitation are the dominant factors moderating maximum temperatures in Buenos Aires on September 3.** 

Northerly flow on September 2 supported afternoon readings near 21–23°C, but a southwestward-moving low-pressure system and frontal boundary are expected to shift winds westerly, increase cloud cover, and deliver showers or thunderstorms overnight into the day. This advection of cooler maritime air limits diurnal warming, with official and ensemble guidance converging on daytime highs of 17–19°C (roughly 63–66°F) under mostly cloudy skies and moderate westerly winds of 15–25 km/h. September climatology places the long-term average maximum near 19°C, so the current setup represents a modest negative anomaly. Model spread in frontal timing creates the narrow uncertainty reflected in market-implied odds favoring 19°C (56%) over 20°C (33.5%), with lower probabilities assigned to 18°C and below. Updated runs from agencies such as the Servicio Meteorológico Nacional will be the key near-term catalyst for any further probability shifts.
